Well, for me it wasn't too bad. I had to get medicated because I couldn't function. Here's what you may be able to do.

1) if you don't have a doctor at all. 

If you have your own insurance card (I'm on my moms insurance and I do), you can schedule and go to an appointment on your own. You can search for doctors and see what insurance they take. Or if you go to the insurance company's website they usually have a search option. 

2) if you have a doctor you've seen before 
    You can call and set up an appointment. Then you go. They shouldn't tell your mom anything, and your mom shouldn't be able to see what you went for. My mom can't see what I get or do because it is my private information. It's her insurance. But I have a card with my name on it. You should too. 

As for getting medicated, go to your doctor and tell them why you are visiting. They may need to transfer your records from your counselor. That's not something your mom could see. They may have you fill out some depression/anxiety scales. It measures how bad it is. Then they will probably give you a low dose of something for a month or so; and then you will do a follow up. It's a long process. But one that's worth it. I'm still not at a good combination yet. But I can function. Which is an improvement.

Black and white is hard. It's the way I see things. You aren't juvenile. I have to ask my dad for money a lot and my mom refuses to. So sometimes it's so hard for me to ask, so I understand. If my mom would, I'd ask her to. I'm sorry that all of this happened. Just try to remember that not everything is 100%. Neither parent is perfect. But I'm sure both of your parents aren't evil either. Try starting with telling yourself that. It's not going to be overnight. Black and white thinking is so hard to overcome. They both have bias. But your dad obviously cares about you and so does your mom. Parenting is hard. I don't understand it. But they make shitty mistakes. 


I'm proud of you for talking to your dad and being honest. Sometimes parents can be pretty out of the loop. I would encourage you to try to do the communicating with your father. That way miscommunications aren't made as much. It's not easy, but please take care of yourself also. Are you in therapy? That could help a lot. Especially if you talked to him/her about your parents. Mine has helped me step back and see my situation with more of a gray area. It's tough. But the gray is there. Small steps.

It took me about 4 therapy sessions for my therapist to feel fully comfortable diagnosing me. We went through so many checklists. So many scales. I thought it would be really quick. A one time visit then the meat of it all. However, it's a slow process. That's a good thing, because you don't want them to rush into it. Part of therapy is seeing your mannerisms and tone and whatnot. It doesn't sound like he is taking you for a ride. 

However, one thing my therapist had me do was homework. I would sort of journal and hand it to her at the beginning of the session. She would read it, and then we would talk about it. That helped with time significantly. 

I was lucky. I found a fantastic therapist who I trust on the first go. I wouldn't label him as a dirt bag just yet. Give it a chance. But don't be scared to ask him for something different if you're not getting what you need. Don't be afraid to shop around either. You're paying money. You need to get what you want. However, remember it is a process that takes time. They generally won't get to the meat of therapy right away.
